claim: Chain-of-thought reasoning adds computational cost: generating an answer alone takes about 3 seconds, incorporating CoT adds about 3.5 seconds, and subsequent keyword extraction and scoring add about 3.5 seconds per question.
falsifier: One could measure processing times on other models and tasks to confirm the relative overhead of chain-of-thought and keyword extraction steps.

conditions: Empirical setting as described in the study
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the specific empirical setting and model used in the study; transfer beyond is unestablished.

claim: Integrating machine learning-derived predictors with classical Cox proportional hazards models improves predictive accuracy for chronic kidney disease progression, as reflected by higher C-index and lower Brier scores.
falsifier: On a comparable CKD cohort with time-to-event outcomes, compare a Cox model trained on clinical features alone against a Cox model augmented with machine learning-derived predictors; the augmented model should show higher C-index and lower Brier scores.

conditions: CKD progression prediction in the studied cohort
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Machine learning-derived predictors for Predictive accuracy for CKD
